title: A sharp fs monoid is the lattice part of its rational cone
statement: Let $P$ be a finitely generated integral saturated commutative monoid, written additively [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], and assume $P$ is sharp: $0$ is its only invertible element. Let $G=P^{\rm gp}$, put $V=G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$, and let $C\subseteq V$ be the rational cone generated by the image of $P$, namely the set of finite sums $\sum_i q_i(p_i\otimes1)$ with $q_i\in\mathbf Q_{\ge0}$ and $p_i\in P$. Then: (a) $G$ is a free abelian group of finite rank, that is, it has a finite $\mathbf Z$-basis, so that $g\mapsto g\otimes1$ embeds $G$ in $V$; (b) $C$ is a pointed rational polyhedral cone spanning $V$, meaning that there are finitely many $v_1,\ldots,v_m\in G$ with $C=\{\sum_j q_jv_j:q_j\in\mathbf Q_{\ge0}\}$, that $C\cap(-C)=\{0\}$, and that every element of $V$ is a difference of two elements of $C$; (c) $P=C\cap G$ inside $V$. The case $P=\{0\}$, $G=0$, $V=0$, $C=\{0\}$ is included.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.17, printed p. 101 (saturation), and Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103 (rational polyhedral fan description); the lattice-cone formulation is expanded here. Kato 1994, Toric singularities, is WANTED for the underlying toric monoid argument.

proof.text: Identify $P$ with its image in $G$ using integrality in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Choose finite monoid generators $p_1,\ldots,p_m$. By the presentation of group completion in that node, every $g\in G$ is an integer combination of the $p_j$, hence a difference $a-b$ with $a,b\in P$. Thus $G$ is finitely generated. If $ng=0$ for an integer $n>0$, both $ng$ and $n(-g)$ lie in $P$. Saturation puts both $g$ and $-g$ in $P$. They are additive inverses in $P$, so sharpness gives $g=0$. Consequently $G$ is torsion-free.

source.place: Agent expansion using Expose VIII 3.1.17, printed p. 101 (saturation); compare Expose VI 3.7(a), printed p. 75.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free] to the finitely generated torsion-free abelian group $G$ established in Step 1. It gives $r\in\mathbf N$ and a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$: every $g$ is uniquely $\sum_k n_ke_k$ with $n_k\in\mathbf Z$. This proves the finite-free assertion in (a).

source.place: Expose VI 3.7(a), printed p. 75, finite torsion-free group completion; the finite-basis result is the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: For each basis coordinate $k$, let $\lambda_k:G\to\mathbf Z$ send $\sum_i n_i e_i$ to $n_k$. The balanced bilinear map $(g,q)\mapsto q\lambda_k(g)$ induces $L_k:G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q\to\mathbf Q$ with $L_k(g\otimes q)=q\lambda_k(g)$. If $g\otimes1=0$, then every coordinate $\lambda_k(g)=L_k(g\otimes1)$ is zero, whence $g=0$. This proves the injection in (a). Also every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors, and $g\otimes q=\sum_k q\lambda_k(g)(e_k\otimes1)$, so every element of $V$ is a rational combination of the $e_k\otimes1$. For $r=0$, the same description says $G=V=0$.

source.place: Agent coordinate calculation from the definition of tensor product and the basis in Step 2; lattice-cone formulation motivated by Expose VIII Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103.

proof.text: Write $v_j=p_j\otimes1$. Each $p\in P$ is $\sum_j a_jp_j$ with $a_j\in\mathbf N$, so substituting this expression into any nonnegative rational combination of elements of $P$ shows $C=\{\sum_j q_jv_j:q_j\in\mathbf Q_{\ge0}\}$. This proves rational polyhedrality with the lattice generators $p_j\in G$. Each $e_k$ is an integer combination $\sum_j b_{kj}p_j$ by Step 1. For $x=\sum_k t_k(e_k\otimes1)$, set $c_j=\sum_k t_kb_{kj}\in\mathbf Q$. Then $x=\sum_j\max(c_j,0)v_j-\sum_j\max(-c_j,0)v_j$, a difference of two elements of $C$. This proves the spanning assertion in (b), including the empty generating family.

source.place: Agent finite-sum expansion of the rational cone; Expose VIII Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103, motivates the combinatorial description.

proof.text: Certainly $P\subseteq C\cap G$. Conversely, let $g\in G$ have $g\otimes1=\sum_j q_j(p_j\otimes1)\in C$ with $q_j\in\mathbf Q_{\ge0}$. Write $q_j=a_j/b_j$ with $a_j\in\mathbf N$ and $b_j\in\mathbf N_{>0}$. Put $N=\prod_j b_j>0$ and $A_j=a_j\prod_{i\ne j}b_i\in\mathbf N$. Multiplying the displayed equality by $N$ gives $(Ng)\otimes1=(\sum_j A_jp_j)\otimes1$. Injectivity from Step 3 gives $Ng=\sum_j A_jp_j\in P$. By saturation in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], $g\in P$. This proves (c); the empty family has $N=1$ and gives $g=0$.

source.place: Agent denominator-clearing proof using Expose VIII 3.1.17, printed p. 101, saturation.

proof.text: If $x\in C\cap(-C)$, write both $x$ and $-x$ as finite nonnegative rational combinations of the $v_j$. Take $N>0$ to be the product of all denominators in both expressions. There are $a,b\in P$ with $Nx=a\otimes1$ and $-Nx=b\otimes1$. Thus $(a+b)\otimes1=0$; Step 3 and integrality give $a+b=0$ in $P$. Hence $a$ is a unit of $P$, and sharpness forces $a=0$. Now $Nx=0$ and $N\ne0$ in $\mathbf Q$, so $x=0$. Conversely $0\in C\cap(-C)$ by the empty sum. This proves pointedness and completes (b). If $P=\{0\}$ then Step 1 gives $G=0$, Step 3 gives $V=0$, and the defining sums give $C=\{0\}$, as required.
